name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible only when focused. This lets keyboard users bypass repetitive blocks like navigation menus, cutting tab stops from dozens to just one or two. The trade-off is a small permanent space at the top of the viewport, but it’s negligible compared to the barrier it removes for screen reader and keyboard-only users.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is the skip link becoming a persistent visual element when focused, cluttering the viewport and breaking the "invisible until needed" principle. A better alternative is a skip link that only appears on keyboard focus, then collapses to zero height when focus moves away, preserving space without sacrificing usability. Settle the argument with a live test: measure tab stops before/after and confirm no layout shift or visual noise remains.
